formatInfo.version: Cập nhật tháng 8/2021 (hiện hành) — Nguồn: ETS TOEIC Speaking & Writing Examinee Handbook (ets.org/toeic)
formatInfo.scoreRange: 0–200 (chia theo các mức Proficiency Levels 1–8; mục tiêu 200 điểm tương đương Level 8 — mức cao nhất)

sections.task: Read a text aloud (Đọc to một đoạn văn ngắn)
sections.criteria: Phát âm (Pronunciation), ngữ điệu và trọng âm (Intonation & Stress). Chú ý ngắt cụm (chunking), nhấn từ nội dung, lên giọng ở đầu danh sách A, B, and C (xuống giọng ở C).

Từ vựng, ngữ pháp, sự mạch lạc. (Lưu ý: Bản cập nhật 08/2021 của ETS đã giảm thời gian nói từ 45s xuống 30s và tăng từ 1 tranh lên 2 tranh Q3–4). Cấu trúc chuẩn 30s: Câu 1 bối cảnh chung → Câu 2–3 tiền cảnh/trung tâm (hiện tại tiếp diễn) → Câu 4 hậu cảnh → Câu 5 ấn tượng chung.

sections.task: Respond to questions (Trả lời 3 câu hỏi ngắn theo chủ đề quen thuộc)
sections.criteria: Trả lời trực diện câu hỏi ngay giây đầu tiên, đúng thì, mở rộng 1–2 lý do/ví dụ thực tế.

sections.task: Respond to questions using information provided (Trả lời câu hỏi dựa trên bảng thông tin/lịch trình)
sections.criteria: Đọc đúng thông tin trên bảng, dùng giới từ chỉ thời gian/địa điểm chuẩn xác (at + giờ, on + ngày, in + phòng). Q8 thường hỏi thông tin đơn lẻ, Q9 thường đính chính thông tin sai của người hỏi, Q10 yêu cầu tóm tắt 2–3 mục.

sections.task: Express an opinion (Trình bày quan điểm cá nhân)
sections.criteria: Cấu trúc rõ ràng (Mở bài nêu rõ quan điểm → Lý do 1 + ví dụ cá nhân/IT → Lý do 2 → Kết luận khẳng định lại), từ vựng đa dạng, liên từ mạch lạc.

items.title: [TOEIC Q5–7 Set 1] Khảo sát thói quen làm việc từ xa (Remote & Hybrid Work Survey)
items.prompt: Imagine that a workplace consulting firm is conducting research on remote work habits. Answer three questions: Q5 (15s): How many days a week do you work from home, and where do you usually set up your workspace? Q6 (15s): What communication tools do you use most frequently to stay in touch with your team? Q7 (30s): What do you think is the biggest challenge of working remotely, and how do you overcome it?
chunks: Q5: I currently follow a hybrid schedule and work from home three days a week...
Q6: I rely heavily on Slack for instant messaging and Zoom or Google Meet for daily stand-ups...
Q7: In my experience, the biggest challenge is maintaining clear communication and work-life boundaries...
To overcome this, I document decisions clearly on Jira and stick to a strict routine
items.sample:
[Q5 - 15s]: I currently follow a hybrid schedule and work from home three days a week. I have a dedicated home office corner with an ergonomic chair and an external monitor so I can focus without distractions.
[Q6 - 15s]: I use Slack throughout the day for quick async updates and code discussions, and we use Zoom every morning for our fifteen-minute daily stand-up meeting.
[Q7 - 30s]: In my experience, the biggest challenge of remote work is avoiding miscommunication when solving complex technical issues. Without face-to-face contact, text messages can sometimes be unclear. To overcome this, I always jump on a quick five-minute screen-sharing huddle whenever a thread gets too long, and I document all key decisions in our shared wiki.
items.tips: Q5 & Q6 chỉ có 15s: trả lời thẳng câu hỏi ở giây thứ 1 + thêm 1 câu chi tiết. Q7 có 30s: nêu luận điểm chính + 1 lý do + 1 cách giải quyết cụ thể.

items.title: [TOEIC Q5–7 Set 2] Khảo sát về phần mềm quản lý công việc (Productivity App Feedback)
items.prompt: A software company is interviewing users about task management apps. Answer three questions: Q5 (15s): How often do you use a digital calendar or task management app, and on which device? Q6 (15s): Do you prefer tracking your daily tasks on a mobile app, a desktop app, or a paper notebook? Why? Q7 (30s): If you could add one new feature to your current project management software, what would it be and how would it help you?
chunks: Q5: I use task management software every single day, mainly on my work laptop...
Q6: I definitely prefer using a desktop web app because I can easily link tickets and code branches...
Q7: If I could add one feature, I would integrate an AI assistant that automatically summarizes sprint progress...
For example, it could flag blocked tickets and save engineers hours of manual status reporting
items.sample:
[Q5 - 15s]: I use digital task management tools every single day, primarily Jira and Notion on my work laptop, though I also check notifications on my smartphone when I'm away from my desk.
[Q6 - 15s]: I definitely prefer a desktop application because it gives me a full view of the Kanban board and makes it much faster to type detailed technical specifications.
[Q7 - 30s]: If I could add one feature, I would build an automated dependency tracker that alerts teams whenever an upstream API change might delay another squad's ticket. Right now, we spend a lot of time manually checking cross-team blockers during stand-ups. Having automatic alerts would save time and prevent last-minute release delays.
items.tips: Ở Q7, câu hỏi giả định 'If you could add...' → mở đầu bằng cấu trúc điều kiện loại 2 'If I could add one feature, I would...' để ăn điểm ngữ pháp.

items.title: [TOEIC Q5–7 Set 3] Khảo sát việc đi lại hàng ngày (Daily Commuting Habits)
items.prompt: A city transportation department is surveying residents about their daily commute. Answer three questions: Q5 (15s): How do you usually get to work, and how long does your commute take? Q6 (15s): What do you usually do to pass the time while commuting? Q7 (30s): What improvements should the city make to encourage more people to use public transportation?

Q6: When I take the bus or train, I like listening to English tech podcasts...
Q7: To encourage public transit, the city should improve bus punctuality and expand metro routes...
In addition, offering an integrated contactless payment card would make commuting much more convenient
items.sample:
[Q5 - 15s]: On the days I go to the office, I usually ride my motorbike, and it takes around thirty minutes each way depending on morning traffic.
[Q6 - 15s]: Whenever I take a taxi or bus, I listen to English podcasts or review my TOEIC flashcards on my phone to make good use of the travel time.
[Q7 - 30s]: I believe the city should focus on two main improvements. First, they should add more dedicated bus lanes and expand the metro network so public transit is faster and more reliable during rush hour. Second, introducing a unified mobile payment app across all buses and trains would make transferring between routes much more convenient for daily commuters.

Q6 (15s): What factors do you check first before buying a new laptop or smartphone? Q7 (30s): Do you think it is better to buy expensive electronics online or at a physical retail store? Explain your reasons.
chunks: Q5: About two months ago, I bought a mechanical keyboard from an authorized online store...
Q6: I always check the hardware specifications, battery life, and verified user reviews first...
Q7: For high-end electronics like laptops, I prefer testing them at a physical store first...
However, I often place the final order online to take advantage of promotional discounts
items.sample:
[Q5 - 15s]: About two months ago, I purchased a wireless mechanical keyboard from an official electronics store online to upgrade my home workstation.
[Q6 - 15s]: Before buying a laptop, I always look at the processor performance, RAM capacity, battery life, and independent video reviews from other developers.
[Q7 - 30s]: For expensive electronics like a laptop or monitor, I prefer visiting a physical store first so I can test the keyboard feel, screen brightness, and build quality in person. However, once I decide on the exact model, I often buy it from the brand's official online store because they usually offer better seasonal discounts and free home delivery.
items.tips: Mẹo Q7: Bạn có thể chọn 1 bên hoặc kết hợp khéo léo (trải nghiệm ở cửa hàng vật lý + đặt mua online để hưởng ưu đãi) miễn là lập luận mạch lạc.

items.title: [TOEIC Q5–7 Set 6] Tham dự sự kiện & hội thảo chuyên ngành (Tech Conferences & Networking)
items.prompt: An event organizer is gathering feedback on professional conferences. Answer three questions: Q5 (15s): How often do you attend professional events, webinars, or industry meetups? Q6 (15s): Would you rather attend a conference in person or join virtually from home? Q7 (30s): What makes a professional conference or workshop valuable to attendees?
chunks: Q5: I attend online tech webinars about once a month and in-person meetups twice a year...
Q6: I prefer attending local conferences in person because networking during coffee breaks is much easier...
Q7: A conference is truly valuable when speakers share real-world case studies rather than sales pitches...
Additionally, interactive Q&A sessions and hands-on coding labs give attendees practical takeaways
items.sample:
[Q5 - 15s]: I join online tech webinars about once a month, and I try to attend major in-person developer conferences in my city at least twice a year.
[Q6 - 15s]: Whenever possible, I prefer attending in person because it is much easier to network with other engineers and exchange ideas during coffee breaks.
[Q7 - 30s]: In my opinion, two things make a conference truly valuable. First, the speakers should share honest, real-world case studies and technical lessons learned rather than giving a disguised sales pitch. Second, there should be interactive Q&A sessions or hands-on workshops where attendees can ask specific questions and apply what they've learned right away.
items.tips: Tránh dừng hình (dead air): nếu cần 1 giây suy nghĩ ở Q7, hãy mở đầu bằng 'That's an interesting question. In my opinion, two main factors make a conference valuable...'

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #1] Quan điểm: Cho phép nhân viên sử dụng công cụ AI trong công việc (AI Tools at Work)
items.prompt: Some companies encourage employees to use generative AI tools (such as coding assistants and writing aids) in their daily work, while others restrict them due to security and quality concerns. Do you think companies should encourage employees to use AI tools at work? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion. (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: In my opinion, companies should definitely encourage employees to use AI tools with proper security guidelines
First of all, AI tools significantly boost productivity by automating repetitive tasks
For example, as a software engineer, I use AI coding assistants to generate unit tests and boilerplate code
Second, providing official enterprise AI tools prevents employees from pasting sensitive data into public websites
For these reasons, I firmly believe adopting AI responsibly is essential for modern workplaces
items.sample: In my opinion, companies should definitely encourage employees to use generative AI tools in their daily work, provided that clear security guidelines are in place. First of all, AI tools dramatically increase productivity by automating repetitive and time-consuming tasks. For example, as a software engineer, I use AI coding assistants to write boilerplate code, generate unit tests, and summarize long technical documentation. This saves me several hours every week and allows me to focus on complex system architecture. Second, when companies officially provide enterprise-grade AI tools and train staff on how to use them safely, employees are much less likely to paste confidential data into unapproved public websites. Of course, human engineers still need to review every output carefully. Overall, for these reasons, I firmly believe that embracing AI tools is a smart decision for any modern organization.
items.tips: Khung 60 giây chuẩn Band 200 cho Q11 (khoảng 130–150 từ): (1) Mở bài trả lời trực tiếp (10s) → (2) First of all + Ví dụ thực tế ngành IT của bạn (25s) → (3) Second + Giải thích tác động (15s) → (4) Overall, for these reasons... (10s).

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #2] Quan điểm: Tuần làm việc 4 ngày (Four-Day Workweek)
items.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Implementing a four-day workweek (32 hours with full pay) would increase overall employee productivity and retention." Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer. (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: I strongly agree that implementing a four-day workweek can boost both productivity and employee retention
First, having a three-day weekend reduces burnout and helps knowledge workers stay mentally sharp
For instance, in the IT industry, tired developers are much more likely to introduce bugs into production
Second, a shorter workweek motivates teams to cut out unnecessary meetings and focus on high-impact tasks
Therefore, I believe a four-day workweek is a win-win for both employees and employers
items.sample: I strongly agree with the statement that a four-day workweek would increase both productivity and employee retention. First of all, knowledge work requires deep concentration, and a three-day weekend gives employees enough time to recharge and avoid burnout. For instance, in the software industry, when developers are exhausted after working long hours, they are much more likely to make mistakes or introduce bugs that take days to fix. Well-rested engineers write cleaner, more reliable code. Second, knowing that there are only four working days forces teams to eliminate unnecessary status meetings and focus strictly on high-priority deliverables. Furthermore, offering a four-day workweek is a powerful perk that helps companies attract and retain top talent in a competitive market. Therefore, I believe a four-day workweek benefits both employees and businesses.
items.tips: Mẹo lấy ví dụ cho dân IT ở Q11: Luôn quy về công việc lập trình/kỹ sư của bạn ('For instance, in the software industry, when developers...') — bạn sẽ nói cực kỳ trôi chảy vì đó là trải nghiệm thật!

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #3] Quan điểm: Làm việc kết hợp (Hybrid) vs. Lên văn phòng 100% (Full-Time In-Office)
items.prompt: Some business leaders believe all employees should return to the office five days a week, while others believe a hybrid model (combining remote and in-office days) is better. Which work arrangement do you prefer, and why? (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: Between the two options, I strongly prefer a hybrid work model over working in the office five days a week
First, a hybrid schedule combines the best of both worlds: deep focus at home and collaboration at the office
When I need to write complex code or debug a system, working from home eliminates office noise and commuting time
On the other hand, going into the office two days a week allows us to hold sprint planning and bond as a team
In conclusion, a hybrid arrangement maximizes both individual efficiency and team cohesion
items.sample: Between the two options, I strongly prefer a hybrid work model rather than returning to the office five days a week. First, a hybrid schedule gives employees the best of both worlds: quiet focus at home and face-to-face collaboration at the office. For example, when I need to write complex backend code or review technical specs, working from home saves me an hour of daily commuting and protects me from constant office interruptions. Second, coming into the office two or three days a week is still enough to build strong relationships with teammates, run brainstorming sessions, and mentor junior developers in person. In contrast, forcing everyone to commute five days a week lowers morale without improving output. In conclusion, a hybrid model is the most balanced and effective approach.
items.tips: Cụm từ ăn điểm Band 200: 'gives employees the best of both worlds', 'face-to-face collaboration', 'constant office interruptions', 'team cohesion'.

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #4] Quan điểm: Chuyên sâu 1 lĩnh vực (Specialist) vs. Đa kỹ năng (Generalist)
items.prompt: In today's fast-changing job market, is it better for professionals to specialize deeply in one specific skill, or to develop a broad range of skills across different areas? Support your opinion with specific reasons and examples. (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: In my view, developing a broad range of skills—while having one strong core area—is better in today's market
First, technology evolves rapidly, so relying on a single narrow skill can be risky if that tool becomes obsolete
For example, a developer who understands backend, cloud deployment, and business communication can adapt to any project
Second, professionals with broad knowledge can bridge the gap between different departments, such as engineering and product
Overall, being adaptable and versatile is the key to long-term career growth
items.sample: In my view, it is much better for professionals to develop a broad range of skills across different areas, often called being a T-shaped professional, rather than focusing narrowly on just one skill. First, technology and business needs change extremely fast. If an engineer only knows one specific framework that eventually becomes obsolete, they may struggle to find new opportunities. By contrast, someone who understands backend coding, cloud infrastructure, and English communication can easily adapt to new roles. Second, having broad knowledge allows you to see the big picture and collaborate effectively across departments. For instance, in my team, developers who understand both technical constraints and customer needs always design better products and get promoted faster. Overall, versatility is the key to long-term career success.
items.tips: Khái niệm 'T-shaped professional' (vừa có chiều rộng đa kỹ năng vừa có 1 mũi nhọn chuyên sâu) cực kỳ tự nhiên và ấn tượng với giám khảo chấm thi.

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #5] Quan điểm: Công ty có nên tài trợ chi phí học tập & thi chứng chỉ cho nhân viên?
items.prompt: Do you agree or disagree that companies should pay for employees' external courses and professional certifications (such as cloud, project management, or language exams)? Give specific reasons and examples to support your opinion. (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: I completely agree that companies should sponsor employees' external courses and professional certifications
First of all, upskilling current employees directly improves the quality of the company's products and services
For example, when my company sponsored an AWS cloud certification for our team, we reduced our server costs by 20 percent
Second, investing in employee growth builds strong loyalty and reduces costly staff turnover
Therefore, educational sponsorship is not an expense, but a high-return investment
items.sample: I completely agree that companies should pay for their employees' external courses and professional certifications. First of all, upgrading employees' skills directly improves the quality and efficiency of the company's own projects. For example, when an IT company sponsors engineers to earn cloud architecture certifications or improve their English skills, those employees can immediately design more secure systems and communicate better with international clients. The money saved from avoiding technical mistakes easily outweighs the cost of the exam fee. Second, investing in professional development shows employees that the company values their long-term career growth. This boosts morale and significantly reduces staff turnover, which is much more expensive than paying for a course. Therefore, sponsoring education is a smart investment for any company.
items.tips: Câu kết đắt giá cho chủ đề ngân sách đào tạo: 'Sponsoring employee education is not merely an expense, but a high-return investment.'

items.title: [TOEIC Q11 #6] Quan điểm: Lãnh đạo nên đề bạt từ nội bộ hay tuyển quản lý từ bên ngoài?
items.prompt: When a management position opens up, some companies prefer to promote an existing employee from within the team, while others prefer to hire an experienced manager from outside. Which approach do you think is better, and why? (Prep: 45s | Speak: 60s)
chunks: In most cases, I believe promoting an existing employee from within the team is the better approach
First, an internal candidate already understands the company's culture, codebase, and business workflows
For instance, a senior engineer promoted to team lead can start making effective decisions on day one
Second, internal promotions motivate the rest of the team because they see a clear career path for hard work
For these reasons, promoting from within is usually more beneficial than hiring externally
items.sample: In most cases, I believe promoting an existing employee from within the team is much better than hiring a manager from outside. First of all, an internal candidate already understands the company's culture, workflows, and technical systems, so there is a much shorter learning curve. For instance, when a senior developer on my team was promoted to engineering manager last year, he already knew our codebase and our clients' expectations, which allowed him to guide the sprint smoothly from day one. Second, promoting from within sends a positive message to the entire organization. When employees see that hard work and dedication are rewarded with leadership opportunities, they feel much more motivated to stay with the company. For these reasons, I think internal promotion is usually the best choice.
items.tips: Cụm từ chuyên nghiệp cho chủ đề HR/Management: 'shorter learning curve', 'from day one', 'sends a positive message to the entire organization', 'rewarded with leadership opportunities'.

items.title: [IT #1] Daily Stand-up: Báo cáo tiến độ, Blocker & phụ thuộc chéo giữa các nhóm (Cross-Team Dependency)
items.prompt: You are in your morning daily stand-up with native-speaking teammates. Give a crisp 60-second update: (1) Yesterday you finished implementing the OAuth2 token refresh logic and unit tests; (2) Today you are integrating the payment webhook; (3) You are blocked on testing the staging endpoint because the DevOps team hasn't whitelisted the new sandbox IP yet. Ask your Scrum Master or DevOps lead for help.
chunks: Yesterday, I wrapped up the OAuth2 token refresh logic and got all unit tests passing
Today, my main focus is integrating the payment webhook and writing integration tests
However, I'm currently blocked on end-to-end testing in the staging environment
We're waiting on the DevOps team to whitelist the payment provider's new sandbox IP
Could someone help me escalate Ticket OPS-312 right after stand-up so we stay on track?
items.sample: Good morning, everyone. Here's my quick update. Yesterday, I wrapped up the OAuth2 token refresh logic, opened the pull request, and got all the unit tests passing in CI. Today, my main focus is integrating the payment webhook handler and setting up the retry mechanism for failed callbacks. However, I'm currently blocked on testing the webhook end-to-end in our staging environment. Specifically, we're waiting on the DevOps team to whitelist the payment gateway's new sandbox IP address in our firewall. I left a comment on ticket OPS-312 yesterday, but haven't heard back yet. Alex, could we sync for two minutes right after stand-up to escalate this so it doesn't delay tomorrow's QA handoff? Thanks!
items.tips: Stand-up với người bản xứ cần ngắn gọn, có cấu trúc 3 phần rõ ràng (Yesterday wrapped up → Today focusing on → Currently blocked on + Call to action cụ thể).

items.title: [IT #2] Sprint Review / Demo tính năng mới cho khách hàng không chuyên kỹ thuật (Non-Tech Stakeholders)
items.prompt: During a Sprint Review, demo a new "One-Click CSV & PDF Invoice Export" feature to non-technical business stakeholders. Avoid heavy jargon: explain the user problem it solves, walk through what happens on screen when they click export, highlight how much time it saves the finance team, and invite their feedback.
chunks: In this sprint, our goal was to make monthly financial reporting much faster for your team
Previously, exporting large reports took several minutes and sometimes froze the browser
As you can see on my screen, you can now filter by date range and click Export to PDF or CSV
Behind the scenes, we process large files in the background and email you a download link within seconds
We'd love to hear your feedback—does this layout match what your accounting team needs?
items.sample: Thanks, everyone. Let me share my screen and walk you through the new One-Click Invoice Export feature we built this sprint. Previously, our finance users told us that downloading monthly transaction reports took several minutes and occasionally froze their browser when there were thousands of rows. To solve this, we redesigned the export workflow. As you can see here on the Billing Dashboard, you simply select your date range, choose either CSV or formatted PDF, and click Export. For smaller reports, the file downloads instantly. For massive end-of-quarter reports, the system processes the file in the background so you can keep working without any lag, and sends a secure download link straight to your inbox within thirty seconds. We estimate this will save your accounting team about four hours every month. I'd love to hear your thoughts—does this cover your reporting needs?
items.tips: Khi demo cho stakeholder không rành code, luôn dùng công thức: Problem (nỗi đau cũ) → Solution on screen (thao tác trực quan) → Business Value (tiết kiệm bao nhiêu giờ/tiền) → Ask for feedback.

items.title: [IT #3] Phỏng vấn System Design: Phân tích đánh đổi kiến trúc (Scalability & Caching Trade-offs)
items.prompt: In a technical interview with an engineering manager, you are asked: "Our e-commerce product catalog API is experiencing high database load and slow response times during flash sales. How would you redesign it, and what are the trade-offs of your approach?" Explain your solution clearly in 75 seconds.
chunks: To handle flash-sale traffic spikes, I would introduce a distributed caching layer using Redis
Since product catalog data is read-heavy and rarely changes every second, caching is a great fit
The main upside is that we can serve 95% of read requests from memory in under ten milliseconds
However, the main trade-off is cache invalidation and potential stale data when prices or stock change
To mitigate this, we can use a short TTL combined with event-driven cache invalidation on inventory updates
items.sample: That's a classic high-read scenario. Since a product catalog during a flash sale has a very high read-to-write ratio, our primary bottleneck is hitting the relational database for identical queries. First, I would introduce an in-memory distributed caching layer, such as Redis, in front of the database using a cache-aside pattern, along with a CDN for static product images. The biggest upside of this approach is that we can offload over ninety percent of read traffic from the primary database and cut API latency down to single-digit milliseconds. However, the main trade-off we have to manage is data consistency—specifically, serving stale price or inventory data, or facing a cache stampede when a popular key expires. To mitigate this, I would keep a short Time-To-Live for general metadata, use event-driven cache invalidation whenever a seller updates a price, and handle real-time stock deduction atomically so we never oversell.
items.tips: Trong phỏng vấn System Design bằng tiếng Anh, người bản xứ đánh giá cao nhất việc bạn chủ động nêu Trade-offs ('The biggest upside is... However, the main trade-off we have to manage is... To mitigate this...').

items.title: [IT #4] Báo cáo sự cố Production & Postmortem (Incident Report & Prevention Plan)
items.prompt: Lead a 60-second blameless postmortem summary for management after a 25-minute checkout outage yesterday afternoon. Cover: (1) Timeline & user impact; (2) Root cause (a database migration locked the orders table during peak traffic); (3) How the team mitigated it (killed the blocking query and rolled back); (4) Preventive action items.
chunks: I'd like to share a quick postmortem summary of yesterday's 25-minute checkout outage
Between 2:10 and 2:35 p.m. UTC, roughly 12 percent of checkout requests failed with timeout errors
The root cause was an unindexed schema migration that acquired a full table lock on the orders table
We mitigated the issue within eight minutes of the alert by terminating the query and rolling back the release
Moving forward, we are adding an automated CI check to block locking migrations during peak hours
items.sample: I'd like to give a quick blameless postmortem summary of yesterday's checkout incident. Between 2:10 and 2:35 p.m. UTC, our monitoring alerted us to a spike in 504 timeout errors, which affected roughly twelve percent of customer checkout attempts. Upon investigation, we found that the root cause was a database schema migration deployed during afternoon traffic that unexpectedly acquired a full table lock on our primary orders table, queuing up incoming writes. We mitigated the impact within eight minutes of the alert by terminating the blocking migration query and rolling back the deployment, which immediately restored normal traffic. To prevent this from happening again, we have two action items this sprint: first, adding an automated linter in our CI pipeline to flag unsafe locking migrations, and second, restricting schema changes to low-traffic maintenance windows.
items.tips: Văn hóa kỹ thuật Âu-Mỹ rất coi trọng 'blameless postmortem' (tập trung vào quy trình và hệ thống, dùng 'the migration caused...' thay vì đổ lỗi cá nhân).

items.title: [IT #5] Đàm phán Deadline & từ chối khéo Scope Creep với Product Manager / Khách hàng
items.prompt: Three days before the sprint release, the Product Manager asks if your team can "quickly squeeze in" a custom role-based permission system before Friday's launch. Politely push back on scope creep, explain the technical risk to the current release, and propose a realistic phased alternative.
chunks: I completely understand why custom role permissions would be valuable for the client
However, adding role-based access control touches every API endpoint and carries high regression risk
If we squeeze this in three days before launch, we won't have enough time for security and QA testing
Here's what I propose instead: let's ship the core release on Friday with standard Admin and Member roles
Then we can prioritize custom permissions at the very top of next sprint and deliver it safely next week
items.sample: I completely understand why the client is asking for custom role-based permissions, and I agree it's an important feature. However, I want to be transparent about the engineering risk if we try to squeeze this into Friday's release. Role-based access control isn't just a small UI toggle—it requires updating authorization checks across fifteen backend API endpoints and writing thorough security tests. If we rush that in over the next three days, we risk introducing critical security bugs or delaying the entire launch. Here is what I'd propose instead: let's stick to our Friday launch with the two standard Admin and Member roles so the client can go live on schedule. Meanwhile, we can scope out the custom permission matrix today and put it at the very top of Monday's sprint backlog. How does that sound?
items.tips: Nghệ thuật Pushback với PM/Client bản xứ: Đừng nói 'No, impossible'. Hãy dùng 'Yes, and here is the trade-off': (1) Đồng cảm giá trị tính năng → (2) Nêu rủi ro chất lượng/bảo mật → (3) Đưa phương án chia giai đoạn (phased rollout).

items.title: [IT #6] Thảo luận Code Review: Góp ý lịch sự để tối ưu hiệu năng (N+1 Query Refactoring)
items.prompt: You are on a quick call with a teammate to discuss their Pull Request. Their code works functionally, but you noticed an N+1 database query inside a `for` loop that will slow down when loading hundreds of records. Praise their clean logic first, then politely explain the N+1 issue and suggest batching the query.
chunks: First off, great job on structuring the new order history service—the unit tests are super clean
I just noticed one performance detail on line 84 that I wanted to walk through with you
Right now, we're calling getUserDetails inside a for-loop, which triggers an N+1 query problem
In staging with ten rows it's fast, but in production with a thousand orders it could cause timeouts
What do you think about collecting all the user IDs first and fetching them in a single batched IN query?
items.sample: Hey Sam, thanks for hopping on a quick call. First off, nice work on structuring the new order history endpoint—the validation logic and unit tests are super clean and easy to read. I just noticed one potential performance bottleneck around line eighty-four that I wanted to discuss. Right now, inside the loop that formats each order, the code calls the database to fetch the customer's profile one by one, which creates an N-plus-one query pattern. In our local environment with ten test records it runs fine, but in production where enterprise accounts load five hundred orders at once, that'll trigger five hundred separate database round-trips. What do you think about collecting all the unique user IDs first and fetching them in a single batched query using an IN clause? I'd be happy to pair with you on it if you'd like!
items.tips: Khi góp ý code review bằng tiếng Anh, dùng câu hỏi gợi mở ('What do you think about...?', 'Have we considered...?') và khen điểm tốt trước sẽ giúp đồng nghiệp rất thoải mái tiếp nhận.

items.title: [IT #7] Giải thích lỗi khó (Race Condition / Concurrency Bug) và xin ý kiến Senior Engineer
items.prompt: You are pairing with a Staff/Senior Engineer to debug an intermittent issue where customers are occasionally charged twice when they double-click the "Pay Now" button on a slow mobile connection. Explain what you've investigated so far, why you suspect a race condition, and ask for their advice on implementing an idempotency key or distributed lock.
chunks: Thanks for taking a look at this with me—I'm debugging an intermittent double-charge issue in checkout
Looking at the logs, two identical POST requests arrive within 50 milliseconds when a user double-clicks
Because both requests read the order status as PENDING before either transaction commits, we hit a race condition
We already disabled the button on the frontend, but retries on flaky mobile networks still slip through
Would you recommend handling this with an idempotency key in Redis or a database row-level lock?
items.sample: Hey Chris, thanks for taking ten minutes to look at this with me. I'm investigating an intermittent bug where a few mobile users were charged twice for the same order. Here's what I've found so far from the logs: when a user is on a flaky 4G connection and taps 'Pay Now' twice, or when the client automatically retries, two identical POST requests hit our API pods within fifty milliseconds of each other. Because both threads check the database at the exact same moment and see the order status as PENDING before the first transaction commits, both requests proceed to call the payment gateway—so it's a classic race condition. We already disable the button on the frontend, but we definitely need backend protection. In our architecture, would you recommend enforcing an idempotency key in Redis, or using a pessimistic `SELECT FOR UPDATE` lock in PostgreSQL?
items.tips: Khi nhờ Senior/Staff Engineer hỗ trợ, đừng chỉ nói 'It doesn't work'. Hãy trình bày theo chuẩn: (1) Triệu chứng lỗi → (2) Bằng chứng từ log bạn đã tìm ra → (3) Giả thuyết của bạn + 2 hướng giải quyết để họ chọn.

items.title: [IT #8] Bàn giao ca trực On-Call cho đồng nghiệp khác múi giờ (On-Call Shift Handover)
items.prompt: Your on-call shift in Vietnam is ending, and you are handing over duties to a teammate in London/US. Give a clear 60-second handover: (1) Overall system health; (2) One noisy memory-usage alert on the reporting worker that you already investigated; (3) An upcoming maintenance window in two hours that they need to watch.
chunks: Hi Jordan, I'm wrapping up my on-call shift here, so let me give you a quick handover
Overall, core production services are stable and error rates have been below 0.05% all day
There is one non-critical alert you should be aware of: memory usage on the PDF reporting worker
I investigated the metrics and restarted the pod; a permanent memory-leak fix is going out tomorrow
Also, please keep an eye on the database read-replica upgrade scheduled in two hours at 14:00 UTC
items.sample: Hi Jordan, good morning! I'm wrapping up my on-call shift on this side, so let me give you a quick handover. Overall, core production services are green and API latency has been completely normal for the past eight hours. There is just one low-priority alert you should be aware of: around two hours ago, we got a warning for high memory usage on the background PDF reporting worker. I checked the profiling metrics, confirmed it wasn't affecting customer traffic, and cycled the pod to free up memory. The backend squad already has a pull request ready to fix that memory leak tomorrow morning. One last thing to keep on your radar: the database team is performing a scheduled read-replica upgrade at 14:00 UTC today. I've pinned the runbook link in the #on-call Slack channel. Let me know if you have any questions!
items.tips: Bàn giao ca trực (On-call handover) cần rõ ràng: Overall status → Active/investigated alerts → Upcoming scheduled changes → Where to find the runbook.

items.title: [IT #9] Họp Sprint Retrospective: Nêu điểm nghẽn CI/CD & đề xuất tự động hóa
items.prompt: In your team's Sprint Retrospective, share constructive feedback: (1) What went well (great collaboration between Frontend and Backend on the new dashboard); (2) What slowed the team down (the CI test suite now takes 35 minutes and fails randomly due to flaky E2E tests); (3) Propose a concrete action item for next sprint.
chunks: First, for what went well this sprint, I want to give a shout-out to the frontend and backend collaboration
Defining the OpenAPI contract on day one saved us a ton of integration rework
On the flip side, one bottleneck that slowed us down was our CI/CD pipeline
Right now, the full build takes 35 minutes, and flaky end-to-end tests force us to re-run builds multiple times
For next sprint, I propose allocating 10% capacity to parallelize our test runner and quarantine flaky tests
items.sample: I'd like to share one thing that went really well this sprint and one bottleneck we should tackle. First, a huge shout-out to both the frontend and backend folks on the analytics dashboard feature—agreeing on the OpenAPI contract on day one allowed us to work in parallel with zero integration surprises. On the flip side, the biggest pain point this sprint was our CI pipeline speed and reliability. Right now, running the full test suite takes thirty-five minutes, and two flaky end-to-end tests failed randomly on almost every pull request, forcing everyone to hit 're-run' two or three times before merging. For next sprint, I'd like to propose an action item: let's dedicate one story to splitting our test suite into parallel shards and quarantining those flaky UI tests so we can get build times back under ten minutes.
items.tips: Trong buổi Retro, cụm từ 'give a shout-out to...' (tuyên dương đồng đội) và 'On the flip side, one bottleneck that slowed us down...' giúp bạn giao tiếp cực kỳ tự nhiên như kỹ sư bản xứ.

items.title: [IT #10] Thuyết phục Ban Giám đốc tách Module Thanh toán từ Monolith sang Microservice
items.prompt: Pitch a technical proposal to engineering leadership: migrating the legacy billing module out of the 8-year-old monolith into an independent cloud microservice. Focus on business & engineering ROI: faster independent deployments, fault isolation, and reduced cloud costs, while proposing a low-risk Strangler Fig migration strategy.
chunks: I'd like to propose extracting our legacy billing module out of the core monolith over the next quarter
Right now, any small update to billing requires redeploying the entire monolith, which slows down releases
Furthermore, during end-of-month invoice generation, heavy CPU usage in billing degrades the main app
By extracting billing into an independent service, we gain fault isolation and can scale it only when needed
To minimize risk, we can use the Strangler Fig pattern and route 5% of traffic first before full cutover
items.sample: I'd like to propose a high-impact architectural initiative for Q3: extracting our legacy billing module out of the core monolith into a standalone cloud service. Currently, our monolith is tightly coupled, which creates two major business problems. First, every time we need to update a tax rule or invoice template, we have to regression-test and redeploy the entire application, delaying feature releases from two days to two weeks. Second, at the end of every month when batch invoicing runs, the heavy CPU spike degrades response times for all active users on our platform. By decoupling billing into an independent microservice, we achieve fault isolation, independent deployment, and auto-scaling that only spins up extra compute during month-end billing—saving roughly twenty percent on our baseline server costs. To keep risk low, we won't do a big-bang rewrite; instead, we'll use the Strangler Fig pattern and shadow-test with five percent of traffic first.
items.tips: Khi thuyết phục lãnh đạo (Engineering Leadership) duyệt dự án kỹ thuật / trả nợ kỹ thuật (Tech Debt), luôn quy đổi lợi ích kỹ thuật sang lợi ích kinh doanh: tốc độ ra tính năng (time-to-market), độ ổn định cho khách hàng (fault isolation), và chi phí hạ tầng (cost savings).
